subject: physiology
title: Metabolic Alkalosis, Respiratory Disorders, and the Anion Gap

steps.tx: Elevation of arterial plasma bicarbonate above twenty-six milliequivalents per litre accompanied by an arterial pH exceeding seven point four five defines clinical **metabolic alkalosis**. It arises from excessive hydrogen ion loss (vomiting, nasogastric suction), exogenous alkali administration, or profound volume contraction with secondary hyperaldosteronism.
steps.say: Metabolic alkalosis is defined by elevated bicarbonate and arterial pH, caused by vomiting, alkali ingestion, or volume depletion.

left.title: Saline-Responsive Alkalosis
points: Urinary chloride concentration < 20 mEq/L
Caused by vomiting, gastric suction, or remote diuretic use
Maintained by extracellular volume depletion and secondary aldosteronism
Promptly corrects with intravenous isotonic sodium chloride

right.title: Saline-Resistant Alkalosis
points: Urinary chloride concentration > 20 mEq/L
Caused by primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn), Cushing, or Bartter/Gitelman
Normal or expanded extracellular volume with hypertension
Refractory to saline infusion; requires mineralocorticoid blockade

steps.tx: Respiratory compensation for metabolic alkalosis involves hypoventilation to retain carbon dioxide. According to clinical compensation rules, for every one milliequivalent per litre rise in plasma bicarbonate, arterial carbon dioxide tension rises by approximately zero point seven millimetres of mercury, defined by **expected respiratory compensation**.
steps.say: Respiratory compensation for metabolic alkalosis raises carbon dioxide by zero point seven millimetres of mercury per unit of bicarbonate.

rows: Δ [HCO3-] = 1 mEq/L per 10 mmHg rise in PaCO2
Δ [HCO3-] = 3.5 mEq/L per 10 mmHg rise in PaCO2

steps.tx: Alveolar hypoventilation caused by central nervous system depression, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or neuromuscular chest wall paralysis produces acute or chronic **respiratory acidosis**. Rising carbon dioxide drives carbonic acid formation, lowering arterial pH; renal compensation reabsorbs bicarbonate and excretes ammonium over several days.
steps.say: Alveolar hypoventilation produces respiratory acidosis, where high carbon dioxide lowers pH until renal bicarbonate retention compensates.

nodes.label: Arterial Carbon Dioxide Rises (PaCO2 > 45 mmHg), Forming Carbonic Acid
Acute Unbuffered Drop in Arterial pH (Acute Respiratory Acidosis)
Renal Tubules Excrete H+ and Retain HCO3- over 48 to 72 Hours (Chronic Compensation)

steps.tx: Conversely, alveolar hyperventilation triggered by severe anxiety, early salicylate intoxication, or high-altitude hypoxaemia expels carbon dioxide rapidly, producing systemic **respiratory alkalosis**. In physiological response, kidneys downregulate proximal bicarbonate reabsorption and type B intercalated cells secrete bicarbonate into urine, gradually restoring the twenty-to-one ratio.
steps.say: Hyperventilation drives carbon dioxide down to cause respiratory alkalosis, corrected by renal bicarbonate excretion.

left.title: Acute Respiratory Alkalosis
points: Immediate onset from anxiety hyperventilation or panic attack
PaCO2 drops below 35 mmHg; pH rises rapidly above 7.45
Cellular buffers release H+; [HCO3-] falls by 2 mEq/L per 10 mmHg drop in PaCO2
Produces ionized hypocalcaemia causing carpopedal spasm

right.title: Chronic Respiratory Alkalosis
points: Sustained exposure to high-altitude hypobaric hypoxia
Renal compensation excretes bicarbonate over 2 to 3 days
[HCO3-] falls by 4 to 5 mEq/L per 10 mmHg drop in PaCO2
Normalizes arterial pH despite persistently low carbon dioxide

steps.tx: In evaluating metabolic acidosis, calculating the difference between unmeasured serum anions and unmeasured cations defines the **serum anion gap**. Calculated as serum sodium minus the sum of serum chloride and bicarbonate, the normal reference value ranges between eight and twelve milliequivalents per litre.
steps.say: The serum anion gap subtracts chloride and bicarbonate from sodium, normally measuring eight to twelve milliequivalents per litre.

left.title: Serum Anion Gap (AG)
points: Formula: AG = [Na+] - ([Cl-] + [HCO3-])
Normal reference range: 8 to 12 mEq/L
Unmeasured anions exceed unmeasured cations
Major contributor is polyanionic serum albumin (~2.5 mEq/L per g/dL)

right.title: Albumin Correction
points: Hypoalbuminaemia falsely lowers baseline anion gap
Correction formula: Adjusted AG = Measured AG + 2.5 × (4.0 - Albumin)
Prevents missing occult ketoacidosis or lactic acidosis in ICU
Critical diagnostic adjustment in cirrhosis and nephrotic syndrome

steps.tx: Elevation of the anion gap above twelve milliequivalents per litre indicates accumulation of unmeasured organic acids, establishing a **high anion gap metabolic acidosis**. Classic causes are remembered by the mnemonic GOLDMARK: glycols, oxoproline, L-lactate, D-lactate, methanol, aspirin, renal failure, and ketoacidosis.
steps.say: A high anion gap acidosis indicates accumulation of unmeasured organic acids, such as lactate, ketones, or toxic alcohols.

rows: Absolute insulin deficiency, infection, missed doses
Circulatory shock, cardiac arrest, severe sepsis
Ingestion of windshield wiper fluid or antifreeze

steps.tx: When metabolic acidosis occurs without unmeasured anions, bicarbonate loss is reciprocally balanced by increased serum chloride retention, generating a **normal anion gap metabolic acidosis**. Common clinical etiologies include severe secretory diarrhea (loss of intestinal bicarbonate) and renal tubular acidosis, both exhibiting hyperchloremia.
steps.say: Normal anion gap acidosis involves hyperchloremia, seen when bicarbonate is lost through diarrhea or renal tubular acidosis.

vis.caption: High anion gap versus normal anion gap hyperchloremic acidosis classification.

steps.tx: The quantity of strong acid or base required to titrate whole blood back to pH seven point four zero at a carbon dioxide tension of forty millimetres of mercury is the **standard base excess**. Negative base excess indicates metabolic acidosis with buffer depletion, whereas positive base excess confirms primary metabolic alkalosis.
steps.say: Standard base excess quantifies buffer surplus or deficit, providing a clear clinical measure of metabolic derangements.
